reviewStandard: Current identity, rank, and NCBI Taxonomy identifiers were checked against NCBI Taxonomy and current nomenclatural authorities, with conservative appearance bounded by primary taxonomic literature, primary microscopy, or referenced type-strain records. The duplicate Clostridium difficile route was initially withheld; control subsequently merged it into the current Clostridioides difficile record as an audited asset-free 308 alias, so the obsolete slug remains excluded from the registry and image sitemap. Clostridium symbiosum remains the validly published correct and medically recommended name in LPSN and the current NCBI name for Taxonomy ID 1512; Enterocloster symbiosus is not an authoritative replacement, while the GTDB-oriented Otoolea symbiosa name lacks nomenclatural standing. Exactly one built-in generation call was made for each of the five supported routes, followed by exactly one control-authorized Clostridioides difficile revision call after v1 was rejected for containing no visible endospores. The type-strain record supports a rod-shaped spore-forming organism, and the selected primary morphology record supports restrained oval subterminal spores with slight sporangial distension. Every copied PNG was inspected at original 1536 by 1024 resolution and visible bodies, spatial groupings, and spores were reconciled without trusting prompt counts. Control accepted Clostridioides difficile v2 and the unchanged Clostridium, C. butyricum, C. perfringens, and C. symbiosum originals. Only those five exact accepted originals are eligible for promotion; v1 remains rejected review evidence and must never become a canonical master.

revisionLinkage.replacementReason: Control rejected v1 because its otherwise clean vegetative-rod plate contained no visible endospores and was too generic for the species page. The sole authorized revision requested two restrained oval subterminal internal endospores.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy and LPSN recognize Clostridioides difficile as current species NCBITaxon:1496. The referenced type-strain record supports a rod-shaped spore-forming organism, while the selected primary morphology record describes large oval subterminal spores with slight sporangial distension. Revision 2 therefore shows only two restrained internal subterminal spores among otherwise vegetative rods, without a lifecycle, universal sporulation, or morphology-only diagnostic claim.
assets.visualReview: Exactly ten elongated rod bodies appear in eight separated groupings: six isolated single rods and two touching two-rod pairs. This is two more bodies and two more groupings than the v2 prompt requested. Exactly two single rods each contain one clearly visible oval internal body in a subterminal position; the other eight rods are vegetative. Spore-bearing rods are not exaggeratedly swollen. No free spore, terminal or central spore, appendage, capsule, halo, shared envelope, host material, disease scene, process sequence, labels, text, scale bar, scenery, clipping, or watermark is visible.
